title: Reject workspace search commands without a query
goal: Prevent a bare workspace-search command with no search term from being executed as a successful search for the command words themselves.
context: The workspace search parser accepts prefixed queries, but a bare phrase such as “tìm kiếm trong workspace” or “Search workspace” currently falls through as a non-empty literal query and can return a verified empty result instead of rejecting malformed Skill input. The first M3 run exposed a related normalization issue: `chatInputText` intentionally preserves ordinary prompts, so a polite lead-in such as “Hãy” can reach the search adapter unchanged and bypass the empty-command guard. Search parsing must strip only recognized polite lead-ins before matching its explicit command grammar.
forbidden_changes: Do not weaken workspace path or secret filtering.
Do not change Skill executor identity binding, policy, or output verification.
Do not alter answer-only chat fallback for genuinely unrelated requests.
acceptance_criteria: Recognized Vietnamese and English search commands with no query fail as malformed even when preceded by a known polite lead-in.
Search commands with explicit non-empty terms still return verified results.
Ambiguous and unsupported intents remain fail-closed.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
A valid search query with a known polite lead-in extracts only the query text and still returns verified results.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: Revert the single squashed task commit if empty-query handling changes valid search behavior; keep the exact empty-command guard ahead of prefix parsing.
